Yes except that requirements need not cite the authors, because the projections of intent are treated more like consensus.  In areas where there is no consensus, it can identify authors and different views but the most common case will be agreement and requirements written as if there is consensus.

I'm thinking identity would come from onboarding, 'what shall I call you' with a default that is inferred from claude code settings so most of the time during onboarding the user can just accept the suggestion.

Relayed intent should record who is being claimed and who the intent is being attributed to, or disagreements might get ugly.  Even though it is not intended to be a security mechanism, it should default to non-impersonation.

Agreement is just a new entry.  Existing entries in both projects can be attributed to me, as "Jamie Kawabata" in both projects.

Any other questions or concerns?
